newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end weaker on fall in U.S., golds.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end weaker on fall in U.S., golds.

text.p: * Toronto stocks end weaker in thin trade, hurt by golds and a second day of losses in the U.S. sparked by interest rate fears.*Volume was 55.27 million shares worth C$629.77 million.
Toronto stocks closed weaker in thin trade on Friday, hurt by weak gold issues and further inflation-related jitters in the U.S. equity markets, traders said.

"The (U.S.) July factory orders which were up 1.8 percent seem to have reignited the fears that maybe there's going to be some inflation and maybe we're going to have to do something about it," said Fred Ketchen, director of equity trading with ScotiaMcLeod Inc.
The TSE 300 Composite Index eased 19.43 points to 5143.40 in turnover of 55.27 million shares worth C$629.77 million.
Declines led advances 441 to 385, with 315 issues flat.

Both Canadian and U.S. bond markets tumbled after the release of stronger-than-expected U.S. economic data on Friday, including the factory orders data and a report showing the Chicago Purchasing Managers August index rose to 60 from 51.2 in July.
The action in bonds helped pull stocks lower on both sides of the border.
* Consolidated Eurocan Ventures Ltd shares rose 0.60 to 6.85 rising in heavy trading on interest generated from an ongoing road show.

* Rogers Communications Inc shares continued to lose ground despite a meeting between Rogers executives and institutional accounts this morning designed to reassure that the company will continue to address its debt-load problems, traders said.
Rogers shares dropped 0.60 to 9.90 in relatively active dealings.
